## Summary

The task required a `DeadlineAlert.matches_definition(other)` method plus correct persistence behavior when DAGs with deadlines are (re-)serialized. The ORM model, `get_by_id`, float-interval storage, and stable-UUID reuse already existed — but two gaps remained.

A method mirroring `__eq__`'s field comparison (`reference`, `interval`, `callback_def`) but returning **`NotImplemented`** (not `False`) when `other` isn't a `DeadlineAlert`, so callers can distinguish "different definition" from "not comparable."

### 2. Made deadline UUID reuse conditional — `serialized_dag.py`
`write_dag` previously reused a prior serialization's deadline UUIDs **unconditionally**, which kept hashes stable for unchanged DAGs (good) but meant a changed interval never produced a new hash or new record (bad). I added `_deadline_definitions_unchanged(...)`, which compares each new deadline definition against the stored `DeadlineAlert` records via `matches_definition`. UUIDs are reused only when definitions are truly unchanged; otherwise fresh UUIDs are generated → new hash → new records with the updated interval.

### 3. Gated the in-place-update optimization
The "dynamic DAG" path (no task instances) does a direct `UPDATE` that never recreates `DeadlineAlert` records.
